standard_prerequisites: Formally etale morphism of rings: the unique lifting property against square-zero ideal extensions, namely for every ring R, every ideal I of R with I squared zero, and every commutative diagram from A to A/J and A to R into R/I, there is a unique ring map A/J to R/I making both triangles commute

A valuation ring of an algebraically closed non-archimedean field with J its maximal ideal provides a local ring A with a nonzero proper ideal J satisfying J squared equals J; such a J cannot be finitely generated by Nakayama
EGA 0, Example 19.10.3(i) claims formally etale maps out of quotients behave in a way this example refutes (this was not caught in the later errata lists of EGA)
core_obligations: Let A be a local ring and J a nonzero proper ideal with J squared equal to J, for instance the valuation ring of an algebraically closed non-archimedean field with J its maximal ideal; the quotient map A to A/J is not flat since J is not finitely generated and the map is not flat by the local criterion for flatness at the closed point

Given a commutative diagram with A to A/J on the left and A mapping by phi to R with I an ideal of R whose square is zero, the map phi sends J into I: phi of J equals phi of J squared which lands in the square of the ideal generated by phi of J in R, contained in I squared, which is zero
Therefore A to R factors uniquely through A/J, supplying the unique lift against the square-zero extension R to R/I; this verifies the formally etale lifting property

Hence there exist formally etale nonflat ring maps, refuting the final sentence of EGA 0, Example 19.10.3(i) and the formally etale case of EGA IV, Theorem 18.4.6(i); part (ii) of that theorem, which is the case used in practice, is not refuted, and the error in the EGA proof is traced to invoking the incorrect EGA 0, Example 19.3.10(i)
proof_roadmap: Set up the quotient by an idempotent nonzero proper ideal J
Check the unique lifting against square-zero extensions via phi of J vanishing
Conclude the formally etale nonflat phenomenon and its EGA consequences
